Definition: from Γαδαρά (a town east of the Jordan); a Gadarene or inhabitant of Gadara:--Gadarene.
BiblicalUsage: Gadarene is the word for a man of Gadara, east of the Jordan, and it stands in Matthew 8:28, where Jesus met two men possessed with devils coming out of the tombs. The King James says the country of the Gergesenes there, following a different manuscript reading, while the Greek text behind most modern Bibles reads Gadarenes. Either way, the place is the far side of the lake, Gentile country, where Jesus cast out demons.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe it matters that Jesus crossed the lake to Gentile country for two tormented men; the name of the town is disputed in the manuscripts, but the mercy is not: He came to them, and I hold that no one is too far across the water for Him.
